India's biggest brands just hit fifty two week lows. Is that a bargain, or a warning? Let's check why they fell.
First, the market. The Nifty is about fourteen percent below its high. But these giants have fallen much harder.
Hindustan Unilever. Down thirty two percent from its high. Profits slipped, input costs are rising, and it has raised detergent prices.
Maruti Suzuki. Down thirty five percent, even though September sales jumped. The market is watching margins, and Q2 results come on October twenty seven.
D Mart. Down thirty two percent. Revenue grew eighteen percent, but margins narrowed, and brokerages cut their targets.
Swiggy. Down fifty nine percent from its high. It fell seventeen percent in a single day, after Instamart losses widened.
N T P C. Down twenty eight percent. It is planning nuclear and green power, but coal supply and big spending are on investors' minds.
So remember, a fifty two week low is not a discount sticker. Ask three questions. Why did it fall? Are profits still growing? Is the debt under control?
Cheap can get cheaper. Save this, and follow moneyincloud. Education only, not investment advice. So, bargain, or warning?
